Crotoxin binds specifically to guinea-pigs (Cavia porcullus) brain tissue and that the binding is not due to phospholipase activity.
crotoxin, a presynaptic neuro-toxin from Crotulus durissus terrificas, binds to brain synaptosomal membranes and whole synaptosomes with a high affinity and specificity.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of specific binding sites in the nervous system for crotoxin, a presynaptic neuro-toxin from the venom of the South American rattlesnake, Crotalus durisus terrificus.
the identification and characterization of crotoxin receptors in the central nervous system and with the determination of their role in neurotoxin-induced neurotoxicity.
the elucidation of the mechanism of action of presynaptic neurooxins, especially crotoxin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(1) crotoxin, a phospholipase, has a high affinity binding site in brain synaptosomes, (2) the binding site has a high affinity for other phospholipase containing neurotoxins from snake venoms, (3) the binding site is located on the external face of the membrane, (4) the binding site appears to be a glycoprotein, and (5) the binding of crotoxins is not dependent upon calcium.

crotoxin and other strong presynaptic neurooxins have high affinity binding sites in synaptosomal membranes which are distinct from the phospholipase sites of the basic subunit of crootoxin and other phospholipases.
